subject: Optimize WATCH by equalStringObjects early length check  (#2107)
reason: The change adds an early length-check short-circuit to equalStringObjects(): when both objects are sds-encoded and sdslen differs, it returns 0 without calling compareStringObjects(). This is semantically identical to the old path, since compareStringObjects() always returns non-zero for sds strings of different lengths (memcmp over the common prefix, or alen-blen as tiebreaker), and both paths are binary-safe.
